questions.question: When is a linear program called infeasible?
options: When no single point satisfies all of its constraints
When its objective can be made larger than any bound
When the origin violates at least one of its constraints
When every feasible point gives a negative objective value

questions.question: An LP has two constraints, each of which can be satisfied by some nonnegative point on its own. What can be concluded about the feasibility of the LP?
options: The LP is feasible, since each constraint has points
The LP is infeasible, since two constraints compete
Nothing yet: their common region may still be empty
The LP is feasible if the objective is bounded

questions.question: An LP with constraints $x_1+x_2\le40$, $x_1+x_2\ge60$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ is infeasible. A planner proposes changing the objective from $\max\ 3x_1+2x_2$ to $\min\ x_1$. What happens to infeasibility?
options: It disappears, since a minimum of $x_1$ always exists
It disappears, as $x_1$ can now be set to $0$
It remains: the constraints have no common point
It becomes an unbounded objective instead of infeasible

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an infeasible LP from an LP with an unbounded objective value?
options: An unbounded LP has feasible points; an infeasible one has none
Both have empty feasible regions but differ in their objectives
An infeasible LP has an unbounded feasible region
Both mean that the simplex method finds no optimal value

questions.question: For an LP with constraints $x_1+2x_2\ge4$, $x_1+x_2\le5$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the origin $(0,0)$ violates the first constraint. What does this show about the LP?
options: The LP is infeasible, since the starting point $(0,0)$ fails
The LP is feasible only after dropping $x_1+2x_2\ge4$
The LP is feasible only with an artificial $R_1>0$ kept
Nothing: the point $(4,0)$ satisfies both constraints

questions.question: Each system below also requires $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Which system is infeasible?
Consider $x_1+2x_2\le4$, $2x_1+3x_2\ge9$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$. What is the largest value of $2x_1+3x_2$ under the first constraint and the sign conditions, and what does it show?
options: $8$, so $2x_1+3x_2\ge9$ cannot hold: infeasible
$6$, the value at the corner $(0,2)$, the largest one
$12$, so $2x_1+3x_2\ge9$ can hold: feasible
$9$, at $(0,3)$, so the system is feasible

questions.question: For an LP with two $\ge$ constraints, Phase I of the two-phase method maximizes $r=-\sum_iR_i$ over the constraints augmented with artificial variables $R_i\ge0$. At the Phase I optimum, $R_1=0$ is nonbasic and $R_2=3$ is basic, so $r^*=-3$. What does this tell about the LP?
options: Feasible, because requirement $1$ is satisfied with $R_1=0$
Infeasible, because requirement $1$ has $R_1=0$ remaining
Infeasible: requirement $2$ remains unmet at this optimum
Feasible after setting $R_2=0$ and starting Phase II

questions.question: A model requires $x_1+x_2=5$ and $x_1-x_2=7$ together with $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Is it feasible?
options: Yes: the point $(6,1)$ solves both equations
No: the only solution is $(6,-1)$, which has $x_2<0$
Yes: $(6,-1)$ is a solution, so a feasible point exists
No: two equalities in two unknowns leave no freedom

questions.question: An LP requires $x_1+x_2\le40$ and $x_1+x_2\ge b$ with $x_1,x_2\ge0$, where $b$ is a demand level. For which values of $b$ is the LP feasible?
options: Exactly for $b\ge40$
Exactly for $b\le40$
Exactly for $b<40$
Exactly for $b\le60$

questions.question: In the two-phase method, Phase I ends with optimal value $r^*=-4$. A student proposes to start Phase II anyway from the final Phase I basis. Why does this not work?
options: That basis has a positive artificial, so it is not feasible
It works, but Phase II will find a lower optimal value
Phase II needs $r^*$ to be positive before it starts
Phase II must always start from the slack basis, not from Phase I

questions.question: A production-planning LP with demand and capacity constraints turns out to be infeasible. Which response addresses the cause?
options: Change the objective so that it no longer conflicts
Add a constraint that explicitly rules out the conflict
Switch from maximizing profit to minimizing cost
Revise the conflicting requirements, e.g. lower a demand

questions.question: An LP is infeasible. One new constraint is added to it, and separately one existing constraint is removed from it. Which statement about the two resulting LPs is correct?
options: Neither change can make an infeasible LP feasible
An added constraint may cut off the conflict; removal cannot
Removing a constraint may help, but adding one never does
Either change may restore feasibility, depending on the data

questions.question: An LP requires $x_1+2x_2=6$ and $x_1\ge8$ with $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Phase I uses $x_1+2x_2+R_1=6$ and $x_1-S_2+R_2=8$ and maximizes $r=-R_1-R_2$. What is the Phase I optimal value $r^*$?
A plan must satisfy $x_1\ge3$, $x_2\ge4$ and the capacity constraint $2x_1+x_2\le c$, where $c$ is the available capacity. What is the smallest $c$ for which the plan is feasible?

A firm must make at least $20$ units of product A ($0.5$ h each) and at least $15$ units of B ($1$ h each), using at most $24$ machine hours; $x_A,x_B\ge0$ are the units. Is this production LP feasible?
options: Yes: $35$ units fit in $24$ h at $0.5$ h each
No: $35$ units need $35$ h, more than $24$
Yes: each lower bound alone fits within $24$ h
No: the minimum plan needs $25$ h, above $24$

questions.question: During Phase I of the two-phase method, which maximizes $r=-\sum_iR_i$, an intermediate tableau shows $r=-3$ while the objective row still has a negative coefficient. What can be concluded about the original LP?
options: It is infeasible, since $r=-3$ is already negative
Nothing yet; only an optimal $r^*<0$ proves infeasibility
It is feasible, since $r$ can still be increased to $0$
It is infeasible if $3$ exceeds the number of artificials

questions.question: An LP has three constraints, and every pair of them can be satisfied together by some nonnegative point. Must the LP be feasible?
options: No: three constraints can conflict although each pair fits
Yes: pairwise compatible constraints are jointly compatible
Yes, provided the LP has only two variables
No, and then dropping any constraint keeps it infeasible

questions.question: The system $2x_1+x_2\le2$, $3x_1+4x_2\ge12$ is infeasible when $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Suppose $x_1$ may take any real value while $x_2\ge0$ is kept. Which point then satisfies both constraints?
The model $x_1+x_2=4$, $2x_1+2x_2=9$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ is fed to Phase I with $x_1+x_2+R_1=4$, $2x_1+2x_2+R_2=9$, maximizing $r=-R_1-R_2$. What is the Phase I optimal value $r^*$?
